ROLE: Design one coherent art-directed collection for EACH provided ten-slot blueprint. The application already chose categories and joint composition patterns from the entire source corpus and retrieved matching reference images. You are NOT selecting a source set, category counts or a new style. In ONE response provide the shared concept, resolved lighting, materialTreatment, paletteRhythm, and exactly ten distinct subjects with descriptions, composition and paletteRole bound to their zero-based slot indices. Choose subjects that NATURALLY fit the given slot: do not force a grounded subject to float, a spatial scene to be flat, or a subject into an incompatible background. All ten subjects must tell one concrete connected story with complementary roles, materials and silhouettes; see all slots together. Preserve producer theme, restrictions and gold mode. Never mention primary/reserve bookkeeping. A category-5 slot requires its declared number of acting characters; ordinary slots require zero. compatibleComposition states genuinely natural allowed support/backdrop/pattern/depth/contextDensity values for that subject, not a dishonest copy of impossible requirements. Describe real light direction, softness, highlights, shadows, materials, colors, scale, placement and framing in the canonical style. Use the attached catalogue references as visual grounding, never copy their subjects, typography, frames or layouts. Return exactly {{setCount}} sets with variantIndex matching input order and every slot index exactly once. If feedback is supplied, repair the problematic assignment/description while retaining the valid story and slots. Canonical rendering rules: {{rules}}. Category definitions: {{categories}}. Producer brief: {{brief}}. Fixed slots and existing reference candidates: {{slots}}. Previous rejection: {{correction}}. Return all user-facing subjects, titles, concept, descriptions, composition and paletteRole in Russian; keep schema field names and controlled tag values unchanged. retain stable IDs in metadata.
batchUniqueness: MULTI-SET SUBJECT UNIQUENESS — batch-unique-v1: Plan ALL requested sets together. No subject type may repeat anywhere in this request, including within a set. For EVERY card return subjectType: a short normalized lowercase English snake_case noun identifying its base object type (for example teapot). Use the SAME type for synonyms, translations, color/material/decorative variants and stylistic or genre variants of the same object. A copper teapot and a porcelain teapot are both teapot; never append a set name, slot index, color, material or arbitrary suffix to fabricate uniqueness. Distinct functional object types remain distinct; do not collapse all furniture or all tools into one type. For narrative cards identify the central action/scene type rather than treating every character scene as one type. Subject types are metadata, not user-facing titles. Ensure names and subjectType values are unique across the entire response before returning it. On repair, previousDesign contains the rejected full design and errors identify conflicting set/slot locations. Keep the first valid occurrence, replace later conflicting subjects with genuinely different types that naturally fit their unchanged slots, and preserve all unaffected subjects, stable IDs, stories, lighting/material contracts and slot descriptions. Do not evade rejection by merely renaming an object or its subjectType. Return the complete corrected response.
entityUniqueness: VISIBLE ENTITY UNIQUENESS — depicted-entities-v1: Applies to single sets and multi-set requests. Every independently recognizable main object, interaction prop and acting character may appear in only ONE card in the entire request. Do not build a story around a recurring protagonist or recurring prop. Theme and complementary roles connect the cards. For EVERY card provide subjectType plus depictedEntities, an exhaustive list of visible independent objects/props/characters (exclude intrinsic assembly parts, worn clothing, ground, sky and generic environment masses). Each entity has kind (object or character), identity (normalized lowercase English snake_case), and appearance (concrete Russian visual description). Object identity is its base functional type, shared across synonyms, materials and colors: the same pickaxe, hat or gold nugget must not recur as a prop in a gold scene after appearing on another card. Ordinary cards must include their subjectType as an object identity. For gold cards, subjectType describes the distinct action/scene; depictedEntities enumerates EVERY actor and interaction prop. The number of character entries must equal the locked characterCount. People count as subjects: a solo hero on one card may NOT reappear in a later duo or a different action, costume, pose or camera view. Give each person a distinct identity and visibly different age, face, hair, build and clothing silhouette/color; never reuse a generic moustached male archetype or fabricate new IDs for the same visible design. Make those appearances explicit and consistent in description, silhouette, composition and paletteRole. Source characters are rendering references only. Check entity identities and appearances across ALL ten cards and ALL sets before returning. On repair preserve fixed slots and unaffected subjects; replace the conflicting characters/objects and rewrite all affected descriptions coherently. Never evade uniqueness by merely renaming identities.
